quarterly_data.signal: Head of IR Susie Lisa said Vertex will complete enrollment in its two phase III studies in diabetic peripheral neuropathy (chronic pain franchise) before the end of the year; both are 12-week studies, so data could come maybe by mid-2027. After the agency declined about a year ago to grant a broad peripheral neuropathic pain label from one DPN and one lumbosacral radiculopathy study, Vertex pivoted to a second DPN study, since two studies in any peripheral neuropathic pain category yield that indication. One study has about 1,100 patients across suzetrigine, placebo and a pregabalin arm, the second about 700 patients versus placebo, run at a more limited number of sites experienced in managing the DPN placebo effect. On the NaV1.7/NaV1.8 combination she said the next step is less about waiting on the DPN results than about seeing where the combination itself might go, in both acute and chronic pain.
quarterly_data.figure: two 12-week phase III DPN studies of about 1,100 and about 700 patients; enrollment complete before year end; data maybe by mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said the JOURNAVX field force started at about 100, 150 reps while reimbursement and access were built up, and Vertex doubled that field force in the March-April timeframe of this year as more reimbursed access came online, adding marketing such as directed TV content on streaming services and celebrity spokespeople. She said Vertex is on track to 3x its scripts in 2026 versus 2025, but that even at 1.6 million that compares with 80 million scripts written a year in acute pain, and called it a very complex launch, very different from Vertex's other businesses.
quarterly_data.figure: about 100, 150 reps initially; field force doubled in March-April; on track to 3x scripts in 2026 versus 2025; 1.6 million versus 80 million scripts a year

quarterly_data.signal: IR's Manisha Pai said that if Vertex decides to pursue musculoskeletal pain over time, that is clearly a primary care market and would be a candidate for partnership, while Vertex still believes peripheral neuropathic pain, as well as acute pain, can be served with a specialty commercial model.

Susie Lisa said everything remains firmly on track with good visibility for the November 30th povetacicept IgAN PDUFA date. On competition she said the first mover, Otsuka with VOYXACT, will benefit from being first, but even with strong uptake the numbers are still really small against the U.S. patient pool; Vertex will also go after switchers and aims to have winning share over the long term. Beyond IgAN, primary membranous nephropathy has no accelerated approval pathway, so its phase III is a 104-week study at the chosen 80 mg dose, and Vertex is still evaluating the RUBY-4 data in wAIHA.
quarterly_data.figure: PDUFA November 30th; pMN phase III 104-week study at 80 mg

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa sized the inaxaplin opportunity: the AMPLITUDE pivotal population is about 150,000 patients, and positive AMPLIFIED results in the expansion cohorts would add an incremental 100,000 patients. She said the AMPLITUDE interim analysis primary endpoint is eGFR slope versus placebo, and that confidence stems from the 47.6% UPCR reduction seen at just 13 weeks in the phase II together with AMKD patients' eGFR declining at almost twice the rate of traditional kidney disease patients, so a differential can be shown even at 48 weeks.
quarterly_data.figure: AMPLITUDE about 150,000 patients; AMPLIFIED could add an incremental 100,000; 47.6% UPCR reduction at 13 weeks; 48 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: Manisha Pai on the closed Crinetics deal: acromegaly is a specialty market treated by about 3,000 endocrinologists in the U.S., and Vertex plans to bring its rare-disease commercialization and ex-U.S. reimbursement expertise to accelerate the PALSONIFY launch and expand it globally. Of the potential $5 billion in peak sales, PALSONIFY is seen as a potential blockbuster and atumelnant, now in phase III for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, as a multi-billion dollar asset; updated timelines and accounting and financial information will come on the Q3 call. On atumelnant liver safety she said only one liver enzyme elevation could not be ruled out as possibly related, with reversible AST/ALT elevations, no bilirubin elevation and no Hy's law cases; the data were shared with the FDA and other regulators, which did not ask for changes to monitoring protocols, and Vertex is confident in the safety profile based on the phase II data.
quarterly_data.figure: about 3,000 U.S. endocrinologists treating acromegaly; $5 billion peak sales potential
